lines.text: Shalom alechim, es Zayn Cheshvin, el Rebe, fabreng muchas veces, habló sobre la importancia de Abish Yisroh,
el hecho de que no pedimos lluvia en Yisroh hasta hoy, porque esta fue la mayor cantidad de tiempo que le tomó a alguien regresar de Yerushalayim,
de hacer la peregrinación al Sanador Egel, a su casa, dondequiera que estuviera.
and there's a story with the Rebbe, and I want to share it with people, and I think it will be inspirational, and it can be used.
Basically, it was 1985, I believe November of 1985, and my wife was pregnant with our oldest child, our only son,
Menachem Mendel may be well, he lives in Florida today, and she went to a birthing class. That night, it was Sunday night, 1985,
it was Lail Zayan Cheshvin, it was like last night, Zayan Cheshvin day, the night of Zayan Cheshvin. It was Sunday night,
so the Rebbe was fabrenged, so I asked my wife if usually I would take her, go with her to the class, and wait for her outside and all that,
there was a birthing class, there was tznias and all that. So this time, I said, do you mind if you drive yourself, so I could listen to fabrenged,
so she said sure, and the fabrenged ended, remember, we're in California, Anschlichus, Marin County, so three hours,
three hours, New York is three hours ahead of California, so the Rebbe finished fabrenging about 12 o'clock or so, or 12.30,
I think it was 12.30 more, it was already 9.30 at night, so I figured that the class is, I think it was 7.30 or 8, and by 9.30,
she was usually home, anyway, she wasn't home, it was 12.30 California time, fabrenged finished already, and I'm waiting,
give it a half hour, she's still not home, I get worried, I call a few of my balabatim, and they say you wait more, wait longer,
give it some more time, and an hour passes by, and she's not home, and I get very worried.
De repente la puerta se abre, y mi esposa entra por la puerta con un policía,
and he says, Rabbi, you have what to be thankful to God for, and he tells me the story that she was driving back on the 101 freeway,
a four-lane highway, in the further lane number one, and a drunk driver speeding at 90 miles an hour, being chased by the police,
went right into our brand new Toyota Corolla that we bought, and it was totaled, she opened her seatbelt, she put on her wig, which fell off,
and here she is, a miracle. Naturally, I was very shook, shook up, and I asked Rabbi Reitchick, our mashpia,
Rabbi Shmuel David Reitchick, all of a sudden, I asked him, what's the lesson here, you know, she's a good person,
there's obviously lessons, so he said, I don't know, write to the Rebbe, write to the Rebbe.
Le escribí al rabino, y el rabino le envió una carta primero deseándole que tuviera una relación
and the baby should be well, and then there was the P.S., and the P.S. was,
the lesson from the episode that you wrote to me about,
the greatness of alacrity, of zwizos, of swiftness, schnellkeit, in all matters of goodness, not just teiromitzos,
Siempre que se trate de algo bueno, hazlo con gran zrizus, gran presteza,
This, the Rebbe said, is the lesson. He didn't say how he came to determine that this is the lesson,
pero supongo que, porque le escribí los detalles, recuerdo haberle escrito vívidamente que la unidad conducía tan rápido,
todo lo que te dije. Años más tarde, me di cuenta de que en el momento en que Terebo dijo esa noche,
the Rebbe spoke about Avraham Babayka, which is the idea of Avraham got up very early to bring Yitzhak Gaza Karbon,
the arcade, and he didn't procrastinate, but he did it, he rose early in the morning to do it, because he was going to do a mitzvah for Hashem.
And if you learn the Maimer, really, it doesn't seem that that part of the Maimer is really relevant to the rest of the Maimer.
At least, outwardly it looks that way. The bottom line is, the Rebbe said it.
Me di cuenta de que lo que Terebo dijo en el Maimer de Hashem Avrom Babuika era la idea de srisus,
which was the prelude for the zwizos, the clip, the hap, the negative type of quickness of the accidents of the Rebbe in his Maimer,
which he said in New York, before the accident happened, send the hifuah, the healing before the maqa,
porque Tzadikim adayim levayim, Tzadikim son similares a Dakotash Borchul, etcétera, etcétera,
but meila, just as the Abel, just as G-d does so, so do tzadikim do.
We should niskayom, ha-yom meil, niskayom nasim, these days are remembered, and we need to make, how do we remember them?
We remember them by nasim, by implementing them, maybe so in everyone's life, to implement and to know that the Rebbe,
nuestro Rebe nos ama y piensa en nosotros, y solo tenemos que quitarnos del camino
and everything will be fine and dandy.
Lechayim lechayim lechayim levrochem masiach ahora.
